races.name: Wexford Fillies Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Banner Beauty
runners_data.note: Progressive flat form at 8f converts poorly here — over a sharp 2m1f hurdle trip at Wexford, she is a natural hold-up racer who will likely find herself further forward than ideal given the crowded rear of the field, which tempers confidence despite good-ground suitability.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lass
runners_data.note: Defaulted to the front by the pace map despite genuine hold-up inclinations; ran 8th of 18 at Wexford over this exact trip on good ground last time, carries a fade-in-finish flag, and the Kinirons yard is 0/5 in the past 14 days — a reluctant pace-setter under pressure.

runners_data.name: Tell The Boys
runners_data.note: Best form angle here — won over 16f on good and finished second over the same trip, trainer Queally in solid 14-day form at 3/7; the hood is not noted, and 61 days off is manageable given the strong recent record at this distance and going combination.

runners_data.name: Baby Pearl
runners_data.note: Sole run was 8th of a heavy ground hurdle at Navan in heavy — no good-ground form, no hurdle form beyond that, and 245 days off the track makes her deeply uncertain; De Bromhead's record suggests she could be forward enough, but the lightly-raced flag and fitness query are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Ballyhahill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who has been placed in bumpers and shown mid-division form on soft; the redistribution from hold-up to midfield reflects a crowded rear, but her best hurdle form of 4th (sole placing) came on soft ground, not good — a going switch to good here needs respecting as a concern.

runners_data.name: Felicity Smoak
runners_data.note: Runs prominently in a hold-up guise here through redistribution; Nolan yard is 0/8 in 14 days and her best recent run was 3rd over 20f on good — stepping down in trip to 2m1f may not suit a stayer, and her natural position at the back is compromised by the field composition.

runners_data.name: Kingside Lady
runners_data.note: Only run was a 13th of a large field over 17f on good at Gowran — minimal form to assess, fades-in-finish flag noted, and McConnell yard is 0/25 in 14 days; very difficult to assess, needs to improve significantly on debut form.

runners_data.name: Ribadora
runners_data.note: Consistent in a modest way — four runs all on good, all in 5th-7th range bar a 13th; ran yesterday (1 day ago), which is a significant concern and must be flagged; form has been steady but uninspiring and the freshness question is acute.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins' runner carries a fades-in-finish flag and a tongue-tie; natural hold-up mover redistributed to midfield, and her form includes a C (completed/fell notation) and modest finishes — the tongue-tie is first-time or re-applied and worth monitoring, but overall profile is weak.

runners_data.name: Sonas
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead debutant with no form to assess and going listed as unknown — an unknown quantity in every sense; the De Bromhead yard has strong maiden hurdle form and two runners in this race, so she warrants watching, but cannot be assessed on evidence.

runners_data.name: Staywitherjohnny
runners_data.note: All flat/bumper form at shorter trips (8-9f), making this hurdle debut over 2m1f a significant step up in both discipline and distance; the 58-day layoff and apprentice jockey add to the uncertainty, and bumper form on soft needs translating to good-ground jumping.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Debutante with no form, trainer Rooney 0/1 in 14 days, and going unknown — the tongue-tie suggests a horse that needs restraining or has shown quirks at home; impossible to assess meaningfully on available data, treat as an unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Casheldale Lass is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front despite a natural hold-up style, meaning this race will be run at a measured, uncontested gallop — she will drift to the front by default rather than through genuine front-running intent, which typically produces a steady early tempo that compresses into a stamina test in the closing stages. With no genuine rival pressing her for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be punishing, favouring those who can travel comfortably in behind and pick up off the bridle late. The field contains a pronounced cluster of hold-up types — Banner Beauty, Ballyhahill, Felicity Smoak, and Shakita are all genuine hold-up performers who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is insufficient room at the rear to represent them all — meaning the back half of the race will be congested with horses out of their natural position. This race shape, with a soft gallop set by a reluctant leader, most favours genuine hold-up horses with proven finishing ability in good ground who can travel sweetly through the race and produce a late run — runners with honest form at this trip on similar ground are best placed to exploit the steady tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Casheldale Lass sets a sustainable, uncontested tempo that keeps the race together until the final flight.
scenarios.body: The uncontested gallop means the field travels in a tight bunch, and the race becomes a stamina-and-class test in the final half-mile with horses finishing off at similar speeds; runners who handle good ground and have shown progressive form at this sort of trip are best suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Casheldale Lass Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Casheldale Lass, despite her redistribution to the front, settles well and uses the lack of pressure to build an unassailable lead that is never properly challenged.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to close the gap before the last hurdle, the steady pace paradoxically turns into a wire-to-wire success for the reluctant pace-setter; her fitness edge from racing 27 days ago and course experience at this trip become critical advantages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grinders Land
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a war of attrition on the Good ground and horses racing prominently off the slow pace grind out the finish ahead of the late-runners stuck in traffic.
scenarios.body: The congested midfield of redistributed hold-up types creates interference late, giving the horses who track the steady pace closest first run and enough momentum to hold on; good ground suits those who can maintain rhythm throughout rather than needing a clear run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced debutants or returning runners — Sonas, Willows Word, or Baby Pearl — has been prepared specifically for this conditions race and produces a sharp performance on debut or return.
scenarios.body: A genuinely unexposed mare handled sympathetically by her connections can exploit a modest pace on good ground when the established form lines are modest and the winner's bar is low in a fillies maiden hurdle; the De Bromhead yard has two runners here and form figures in this race are generally unimpressive.

watchPoints.text: Ribadora ran just yesterday (1 day since last run) — monitor for signs of fatigue or stilted jumping mid-race as a horse asked to run on back-to-back days over hurdles.

The congested midfield of redistributed hold-up types (Banner Beauty, Ballyhahill, Felicity Smoak, Shakita) creates a significant traffic-risk scenario from the third-last hurdle — watch for interference or horses failing to find a run at a critical stage.
Casheldale Lass is a reluctant pace-setter — if she is slow to go forward from the gate and another runner takes up the lead, the entire pace map shifts and the shape assumptions become unreliable.

Sonas and Willows Word are both debutantes from established yards (De Bromhead and Rooney respectively) — early market moves on either should be noted as a signal of stable confidence that cannot be read from the form.

Tell The Boys is the only runner combining a win and a place finish at this exact distance on good ground — watch how Kevin Sexton positions him early, as the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/7 suggests the yard is in form.

races.name: Shamrock Farm Enterprises Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: It's Bobsled Time
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 4yo hold-up type whose recent form includes a win and a fall, but whose record on Good ground is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 5 similar-going runs) and who carries a stamina fade flag — 182 days off the track is a further concern for Declan Queally's charge.
runners_data.comment: Long absence of 182 days and a tumble last time make him hard to trust, and he is ranked last on our figures despite that win three starts back; the lengthy layoff is the biggest question mark here.

runners_data.name: Camino Rock
runners_data.note: A 9yo veteran only 10 days off his last run, holding an honest record on Good ground (1W, 1P from 8 similar runs), and Josh Williamson's 5lb claim is a useful aid; sits at the back naturally but has the fitness edge given his recency.
runners_data.comment: Camino Rock has a troubled recent spell — pulling up twice, unseating, and finishing unplaced in his last four starts — yet has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating comfortably heads this seven-runner field. Fitness is not an issue at just ten days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Morell River
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's 6yo has a strong profile on Good ground (2W, 3P from 10 similar runs), including wins at today's trip, and is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — though the crowded rear means he may need to race slightly further forward than ideal to avoid traffic; the style-fit discount applies but underlying form is the most relevant angle here.
runners_data.comment: Morell River has winning form and a second two starts back to her name, and with experience of today's distance and going, she arrives here on a sound overall profile. The main concern is that eighth on her most recent start leaves her needing to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter and the key race-shaper; R P Cody's 5yo has been prominent in his better efforts but has not converted on Good ground (0W, 3P from 9 runs) — his value today is entirely positional, and the style-fit flag is less meaningful given he is genuinely expected to lead rather than being forced to.
runners_data.comment: Harpy Eagle arrives here on a quick 16-day turnaround carrying 161 lb, and with experience of today's trip and conditions, he appeals as a genuine threat at a mark of 100 despite our rating of 115 suggesting he's well treated — the risk is a winless recent run of five starts that will need reversing.

runners_data.name: Marian Avenue
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' 6yo is a natural hold-up runner carrying the stamina-fade flag, and her Good-ground record is modest (0W, 1P from 7 runs) — 72 days off adds a fitness query, and Philip Byrnes faces the challenge of delivering a run from the rear in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to stretch the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Marian Avenue brings going experience to the table but 72 days off the track and a hefty 160 lb to carry are real tests; that disqualification last time out adds a frustrating edge to a profile that promises more than it delivers.

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: A 4yo wearing a hood for the first time, trained by P J Rothwell and ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe — the headgear is worth noting; won over 2m on Good last time out but has since struggled, and while the jockey booking is strong, this is a horse racing out of its natural hold-up role in terms of map position with a moderate style-fit score.
runners_data.comment: Ocean Murphy arrives here in fine heart after winning last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going — the main query is whether 155 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Isdistheone
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's 6yo wears a tongue-tie and is 90 days off the track with a flat recent profile (no wins or places in last 5 runs including on Good ground); Kevin Healy's 7lb claim offers some compensation but the horse's form profile gives little reason for confidence regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 90 days off, Isdistheone faces a stiff ask carrying 147 lb, and our figures rank her sixth of seven; she has run over today's trip and going before, which is at least a genuine positive to cling to.

races.paceDynamic: Harpy Eagle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4f on Good ground at Wexford, and with no genuine rival to press him from the outside, he is expected to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. The remainder of the field is predominantly made up of hold-up horses — Morell River, Marian Avenue, Ocean Murphy, and Isdistheone are all natural closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is insufficient space at the rear to place them all accurately; in reality, the chasing pack will be strung out behind a single pace-setter. Camino Rock and It's Bobsled Time complete a field in which almost every runner prefers to come from off the pace, meaning Harpy Eagle faces no real test of his lead and the tempo is entirely in his hands. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical versatility or a late turn of foot, but the lone, unchallenged front-runner operating at a comfortable clip on Good ground over an extended trip holds a significant positional advantage — hold-up horses must produce a sustained finish from a long way out with no true target-setters to drag them into contention early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harpy Eagle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle bowls along at a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the field fails to apply meaningful pressure at any stage of the race.
scenarios.body: Harpy Eagle controls every fraction from the front, conserving energy through the middle section before kicking for home turning in; with no horse able to sustain a run from far back on a flat Good surface, the leader proves difficult to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Finisher Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Harpy Eagle proves just quick enough to compromise his stamina in the final half-mile, opening the door for a horse with a strong finishing run.
scenarios.body: A runner who has settled comfortably in mid-division — most likely Morell River, who has demonstrated genuine closing ability on Good ground — picks up smoothly off a true enough gallop and gets to the leader close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Gets In
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle fades dramatically in the straight and a horse who has raced prominently rather than from deep proves best placed to capitalise.
scenarios.body: With the field strung out and no sustained forward move from the true hold-up horses, a horse sitting just off the pace in second or third converts the momentum advantage into a winning run late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely strong throughout and the entire front half of the field weakens, allowing a deep-seated closer to swoopfrom off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given only one genuine pace-setter and a cluster of natural hold-up types who will struggle to generate the necessary ground-making run from far back on Good ground over this trip.

watchPoints.text: Harpy Eagle sets the entire race tempo alone — if he is allowed to dictate an easy fractions in the front half, the field may find it impossible to close him down in the straight and he becomes the danger regardless of his modest Good-ground record.

Morell River is the most likely closer to threaten given his two wins on Good ground and course-distance form, but Ricky Doyle will need to position him far closer to the pace than his natural style demands — watch for where he is placed at the third hurdle.

Ocean Murphy's hood first-time application is a live unknown — horses wearing headgear for the first time can race more keenly or erratically, which could disrupt the shape of the chasing pack behind Harpy Eagle in the early stages.

It's Bobsled Time and Marian Avenue both carry stamina-fade flags — if either gets competitive approaching the home turn, watch for them weakening inside the final two hurdles and opening gaps for other hold-up horses to exploit.

The compressed weight range (147–166lbs) and the volume of hold-up types means traffic in the straight is a real possibility — Darragh O'Keeffe on Ocean Murphy and Josh Williamson on Camino Rock are the jockeys most likely to need to navigate around beaten horses late.

races.name: Wexford Racecourse Park Run Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for William Harvey who has a poor recent run of form (U5-U70) and carries a warning flag for fading in finishes; the unseated rider entries raise genuine jumping concerns over 2m3f and Good ground does not appear to unlock this horse based on three runs without a win or place in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Begger is yet to win in recent starts, with a fifth four starts back the best he can show alongside a pair of unseated-rider incidents; unexposed and open to improvement, he carries 166 lb on 11 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins and six places from 13 runs on Good ground, giving him the best similar-going strike rate among the hold-up/prominent group; headgear (p) is noted, jockey Alex Harvey represents a yard on 0/25 in the last 14 days, but the horse's consistency and experience over 19-21f on Good is a genuine asset here.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two starts back and beaten out of sight since a win five starts back, Jackson Lamb carries a hefty 166 lb off a trainer who has drawn a blank in 25 recent attempts — he has run over today's trip and going, but there is precious little here to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Nadia's Boy
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner ridden by Paul Townend for W P Mullins — the standout tactical unit in the race; two wins from four Good-ground starts and a 2W3P record in similar conditions underline his suitability, and with no rival to push him early, he can set whatever gallop he chooses and conserve energy for the jumping battle.
runners_data.comment: Nadia's Boy boasts two wins in his last four starts, with victories three and four starts back, and third last time out — experience over today's trip and going combining with a trainer firing at 26% in the last 14 days to make him the one to beat despite a hefty 166 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Gordon Elliott (headgear: t) who has been placed in four of his last five starts and boasts a 1W6P record from 10 runs on Good ground; ran 2m6f and 2m recently suggesting the 2m3f trip is within range, and a 5-runner claim jockey (Josh Williamson) is a positive at this level.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and rarely out of the frame, Scalpnagoon has run over today's distance and going before and, rated 119, shapes as a genuine threat from a career-high 166 lb — though a trainer firing at just 2% in the last 14 days is the concern.

runners_data.name: West Away
runners_data.note: Collins-trained hold-up horse making a 17-day turnaround, but its natural style places it off the pace — shown in midfield on the map only because more hold-up types exist than rear slots allow, so its true role is further back than visualised; one win from 11 Good-ground starts suggests it needs things to fall right and a strong pace that this race shape may not deliver.
runners_data.comment: West Away shaped with promise when third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call upon; the weight burden of 166 lb looks the main obstacle to him going one better.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David Harry Kelly (headgear: t) who has a troubled recent form string including a U and several poor finishes; 11-day turnaround and a 7-runner claim apprentice (Peter Smithers) soften the appeal, and while he has Good-ground form, the -972U5 run of figures suggests he is not in a consistent spell at present.
runners_data.comment: William Tell has run over today's trip and going, shaped with real promise when a close second three starts back, and at 166 lb he arrives fresh just 11 days on — the main concern is that he's yet to score in recent starts, and the unseating two starts back leaves a question mark.

runners_data.name: Kelya
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Emmet Mullins returning from a remarkable 513-day absence, carrying 2/21 T14 figures suggesting the yard is in fair recent form; her last completed run was a win at 3/18f on Heavier ground, and while she showed ability in a previous Good run (7/22f), the lengthy layoff introduces significant uncertainty over both fitness and jumping sharpness in a steeplechase context.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 513 days makes fitness the obvious query, but her last-five starts show a winner and a placed effort in recent form, hinting at ability worth respecting. Carrying 159 lb on return, she remains unexposed and open to improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Nadia's Boy (Paul Townend, W P Mullins) is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner beginners' chase and, with no serious challenger for the lead, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m3f trip on Good ground. Jackson Lamb and Scalpnagoon will press from prominent positions just off the pace, while William Tell, despite a prominent style, has shown inconsistency and is unlikely to challenge Nadia's Boy for the front early. The hold-up horses — Begger, Kelya, and West Away — will be operating from the rear, though West Away is a genuine hold-up type redistributed into a midfield slot on the map because the field's shape pushes true closers further back than the visual suggests; this field contains more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate, and West Away in particular is unlikely to secure a more forward position than shown. With one dominant front-runner setting an unhurried, measured gallop on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader without burning energy and pounce in the straight, rather than horses who need a strong pace to reel in runners from off the bridle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nadia's Boy Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy bowls along uncontested at a steady pace, Townend dictates terms and kicks clear before the last.
scenarios.body: Nadia's Boy's form figures of two wins at this trip on Good ground, combined with Townend's masterclass in front-running, make this the path of least resistance; the lack of any genuine pace challenger means the leader is never seriously threatened going to the final fence. Prominent types Jackson Lamb and Scalpnagoon finish best of the rest but are outclassed if Mullins' runner is given a soft lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Jackson Lamb or Scalpnagoon applies sustained pressure from the second half of the race and Nadia's Boy's jumping falters or weakens.
scenarios.body: Scalpnagoon's consistent placing record (four times placed in five recent starts on Good ground) and Jackson Lamb's winning form at 21f on Good suit a race where the pace is honest enough to keep them primed for a late surge. If Nadia's Boy makes a costly error at a fence, the prominent pair are best placed to capitalise immediately.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy sets a genuinely stronger pace than expected and ties himself up approaching the last, allowing hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Kelya is returning from 513 days off but showed a win in her most recent completed run and has Good-ground form; Begger, however, is flagged as fading in finishes and may not see out the race strongly. This scenario requires a material pace collapse from the leader — which Nadia's Boy's profile does not strongly suggest — making it a low-probability but live threat if conditions surprise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Implodes — Errors Cost
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy or multiple leading contenders make jumping errors at crucial fences, opening the race up for whoever survives cleanest.
scenarios.body: Begger carries a form string showing unseated rider entries (U) which raises jumping doubts, and William Tell's recent U also flags jumping fragility; in a chaos scenario, the horse who jumps cleanest and is handiest at the final fence wins regardless of style. Scalpnagoon's solid placing record and reliable jumping in comparable fields gives it the best fall-back profile if the favourite exits.

watchPoints.text: Nadia's Boy's jumping must be monitored at every fence — if Paul Townend's front-runner makes a jumping error mid-race, the entire race shape collapses and prominence horses Scalpnagoon and Jackson Lamb immediately become the primary threats.

Begger carries two unseated rider entries in recent form and William Tell has a recent U on his card — in a beginners' chase with seven runners, a fallers' chain or interference incident in the back straight is a live risk that could dramatically alter the shape of the race.

Kelya's 513-day absence is the longest layoff in the field and her jumping in a beginners' chase context must be treated as an unknown quantity; Emmet Mullins' 2/21 T14 record is modest, and if she makes errors, she could interfere with hold-up horses operating behind her.

West Away's redistribution from true hold-up to midfield means any punter expecting it to produce a late sustained run from the rear should note the race shape does not provide the strong pace required — its 1W from 11 Good-ground starts underlines the narrow margin for error if it cannot get a clean run from its actual position.

races.name: Wexfordraces.ie Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, likely to dictate from flag to finish on this good ground; trainer Thomas Gibney has had no winners from 9 runners over the past 14 days, but the horse's profile fits this race shape best and its last two runs over similar trips at Wexford on good ground were encouraging — style fit at 0.93 is a slight flag only if the race shape demands it leads hard.|
runners_data.comment: Leave In Secret arrives here in cracking nick — third last time out and unexposed at this level, he has run over today's trip and going and our rating has him edging the field; the worry is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Freddie Robdal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead in excellent 14-day form (4/31) and this 9-year-old has a respectable record on good going with two second-place finishes in recent history; a hold-up horse who will need the pace to sharpen in the latter stages to deliver his run from off the pace over 2m3f after a 56-day absence.|

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago, which raises freshness questions, and the tongue-bar headgear may aid concentration; a hold-up type whose best form has come over slightly longer trips (24-26f) meaning 2m3f is towards the shorter end, and relies on a truly run race to get competitive from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Beggars Rock showed useful form when third three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour at a competitive weight of 164 lb — though he's been winless in his last five starts and that inconsistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: Rated only 103 but has back-to-back placed efforts over this sort of trip on good ground, worn hood throughout; a natural hold-up horse who sets sail late and needs genuine pace to bridge the gap — carried out/pulled up in two recent starts adds a reliability concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Tequila Talkin' is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before; a pull-up last time out is the chief concern, despite a second and third in between.

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: Showed a good second last time on good ground over 2m, which is the key recent form reference; a true hold-up horse by inclination but the crowded rear means it has been pushed into a midfield projection — its best chance is if it can sit closer than usual on a tight Wexford circuit, though the style-fit flag (0.93) is a real caution.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a pulled-up run sandwiched between modest efforts, Centreofattention does at least return on a handy 17-day turnaround with going experience and a second last time out offering mild encouragement — though 158 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Won over 2m½f on good going in the recent past and that trip form is relevant here; holds up naturally and was redistributed to midfield only because the rear of the field is congested — Anna McGuinness takes a 7lb claim but trainer Sean Aherne has had just one runner in the past 14 days, limiting confidence in stable form.|
runners_data.comment: Oneforgonzo has run over today's trip and going, and a win three starts back shows he can find the frame, but unplaced last time and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, he faces a stiff ask off 157 lb.

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran who has posted consistent efforts around this sort of trip on good ground, though without a win in the last five; races with a patient hold-up style that the pace map could not accommodate, pushing it into a midfield slot — no wins recorded in trainer Eamon Courtney's last 14-day window and the OR of 94 reflects a horse at its ceiling.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time is a concern, but Temptationinmilan had shown better form before that, and with experience over today's trip and going, 22 days' freshness, and a rating of 110 suggesting ability to spare, he shapes as a lively contender here off 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent type likely to be on the heels of Leave In Secret throughout; tongue-tie fitted and only 6-years-old with room to progress in handicap company, but recent form reads poorly (two pulls up, a ninth) and trainer P J Rothwell has drawn a blank in 18 runners over the past fortnight — jumping soundness is a key unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Following Orders has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 108 suggests he holds strong claims at the weights — yet two pulled-up efforts in his last five starts make jumping reliability the key concern for punters to weigh.

runners_data.name: Avec Espoir
runners_data.note: Thirteen years old and returning from 307 days off the track, which is a very significant concern whatever the other merits; a prominent racer who might travel well early, but the extreme layoff combined with age and modest recent form (four last-place efforts) makes it very hard to take seriously at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, including a pull-up, and absent for 307 days — Avec Espoir faces a stiff task returning here, though he has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating of 98 offers a sliver of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner handicap chase and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m3f trip on good ground at Wexford. Following Orders and Avec Espoir are prominent types who may track close behind, but neither has the profile to seriously pressurise Leave In Secret early, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than searching. The hold-up contingent — Freddie Robdal, Beggars Rock, Tequila Talkin' — will be doing their work from well off the pace and will need the tempo to lift in the final mile to generate the ground-closing momentum they depend on. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer able to travel economically in the slipstream of Leave In Secret and pounce turning for home, rather than a pure closer who needs a strong pace to get into it. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Centreofattention, Oneforgonzo, and Temptationinmilan are true hold-up horses pushed into a midfield projection; of those, Centreofattention is the most likely to secure the closest position to the pace given the nature of Wexford's tight circuit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leave In Secret Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret bowls along uncontested and sets a measured, rail-hugging gallop that suits a prominent tracker.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret or the closest prominent follower dictates the fractions, the hold-up horses are left with too much to do from the rear, and a horse racing in the top three throughout pounces between the last two fences. Good ground and a steady gallop reward jumping fluency and economical travel over raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Get Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and Leave In Secret's lead begins to crumble, opening a late run for the hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Freddie Robdal or Beggars Rock, given enough room on the final bend, produces a strong late surge if the tempo has been genuinely testing throughout. Tequila Talkin' is also capable on these terms, having finished second twice at this sort of distance on good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Reshuffles
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent horse blunders or falls at a critical fence, opening space for a midfield tracker to inherit a winning pitch.
scenarios.body: On a tight track like Wexford the complexion can change instantly at any fence, and a horse like Centreofattention or Oneforgonzo, travelling in the midfield pack, could benefit from attrition ahead and suddenly find themselves in a winning position. These horses are natural hold-up types racing closer than ideal, but a reshuffle by jumping errors could accidentally deliver them the position their style fits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret's jumping deteriorates or it ties up late, removing all front-running control and causing a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: Without Leave In Secret holding form, the race loses its shape entirely and the result becomes a lottery among the hold-up and midfield types who have been travelling within themselves. Temptationinmilan and Beggars Rock are veteran types who could capitalise, though their recent records suggest this is a low-probability route to success.

watchPoints.text: Leave In Secret's jumping must be monitored at every fence — if it makes a meaningful error in the first half of the race, the entire pace map breaks down and the result becomes unpredictable, with Following Orders most likely to inherit the front.|

Avec Espoir is 307 days absent and 13 years old; any sign of laboured jumping or early distress could cause interference for the prominent horses immediately behind, most notably Following Orders and Leave In Secret.|

Centreofattention, Oneforgonzo, and Temptationinmilan are all genuine hold-up horses competing for limited rear-field space — watch for traffic problems on the tight Wexford bends, particularly turning out of the back straight where bunching is likely.|

Freddie Robdal's 56-day absence for a De Bromhead yard that has been firing (4/31 over 14 days) is worth noting — if the horse travels smoothly mid-race and is produced with a well-timed run between the last two fences, it is the most dangerous late challenger to a prominent winner.|

races.name: Poolcourt Engineering Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Sphagnum
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer for Broderick with two placing runs over 26f on Good, the 7lb claimer Sampson keeps the weight competitive but the latest form string (080-27) shows inconsistency — Good ground suits and the trip is familiar, but a win hasn't come since those older form entries.|
runners_data.comment: Sphagnum has run over today's trip and going, arrives here 27 days fresh and shaped with promise when second two starts back; the risk is he's been winless in recent starts and will need to recapture that level after disappointing efforts either side of it.

runners_data.name: Rockonliam
runners_data.note: Two wins on the bounce over 20f on Good ground make him the most in-form runner here; De Bromhead and O'Keeffe (T14: 4/31) is a sharp yard-jockey combo and the tongue-tie aids breathing focus as he attempts to front-run over a longer 26f — the stamina extension from his recent 20f wins is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Rockonliam arrives on the back of back-to-back wins but our figures rank him sixth of seven, and 162 lb is a significant burden to overcome; he has experience of today's going, at least, to draw on.

runners_data.name: Jacovec Cavern
runners_data.note: Paul Hennessy's seven-year-old has a solid platform over similar ground with a win at 20f and a second at 22f in recent outings; the 5lb claimer Condon helps at the weights and the pauline form string (01-23P) includes a pulled-up that needs watching, though Good ground consistently brings out a better performance level.|
runners_data.comment: Jacovec Cavern showed real ability when winning and filling the runner-up spot in his last five starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the pull-up last time is the one query, but on a mark of 116 he remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Rue Taylor
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight runs on similar going underlines a real affinity with Good turf, and Nolan's yard has 0/8 in the past 14 days which is a minor flag; the 156lb weight is the lightest of the prominent runners and Staples's 5lb claim helps — the stamina at 26f is a slight step up but the horse has run well over 23f.|
runners_data.comment: Rue Taylor won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making her a serious threat at the head of the market — the concern is whether 39 days between runs leaves her spot-on for this test carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Conor O'Dwyer's five-year-old is a genuine prominent racer by style (1W from 4P on similar going), and in a field stacked with pace, the horse is mapped to midfield through redistribution rather than natural inclination — its chance is best shaped around a scenario where front-runners collapse, but that is not the dominant shape here and its form (245-12) is genuinely progressive.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of our figures, Teenage Kiss faces a stiff ask off 153 lb, and her recent form is patchy — fifth and fourth mixed in with better efforts. She does bring distance and going experience, and was a winner two starts back.

runners_data.name: Ceroc
runners_data.note: Slattery's eight-year-old front-runner arrives on a short 17-day turnaround (T14: 4/40) and the recent win over 24f on Good is a strong tick; tongue-tie and blinkers are familiar headgear, but the two pulled-up runs in the form string (P6-2P1) are a jumping reliability concern over 3m1f — if Rockonliam applies early pressure, Ceroc's record suggests vulnerability late.|
runners_data.comment: Ceroc bounced back to winning form last time out, but a pulled-up effort two starts back raises a stamina or soundness query; he has run over today's distance and going, and at 152 lb he faces a stiff weight task stepping into this grade.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: Flavin's seven-year-old is a prominent horse by inclination but is shown at the rear of the field through redistribution, racing out of its natural role with a style-fit score of 0.84 — the recent form (52F-P5) includes a fall and a pulled-up which are significant jumping concerns at this trip, and the 151lb weight gives little relief.|
runners_data.comment: Duty Bound has experience of today's trip and going, and a second four starts back hints at the ability to compete at this level — our rating of 115 makes him a leading danger despite carrying 151 lb. The concern is his recent run of pulled up and fell, which clouds his current reliability.

races.paceDynamic: Rockonliam and Ceroc are the two confirmed front-runners in this 3m1f handicap chase, and with both carrying handlers who have been in recent form, neither is likely to cede the lead without a fight — a genuinely contested early gallop is the most realistic outcome over this trip on Good ground at Wexford. The honest, pressured pace they create across the early fences will stretch the field and test jumping accuracy, favouring horses who can travel comfortably in behind without expending energy fighting for position. Sphagnum, Jacovec Cavern, and Rue Taylor all sit naturally in the prominent-to-midfield bracket and are best placed to exploit a strong-run race from a stalking position. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Rockonliam and Ceroc are most likely to actually dominate the front rank, with Teenage Kiss and Duty Bound both true prominent racers who will be shuffled into less natural roles. The race shape strongly favours patient, prominent-to-midfield stalkers who travel smoothly in a contested gallop and produce a clean round of jumping late, particularly from the second-last fence onwards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rockonliam and Ceroc burn each other up setting a genuine gallop, leaving prominent-to-midfield chasers to pounce from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners honest gallop depletes their reserves up the Wexford straight, allowing Sphagnum, Jacovec Cavern, and Rue Taylor to pick up the pieces with fresher legs. All three have good similar-going records and the Good surface suits; this is the dominant race shape given the dual front-runner dynamic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rockonliam breaks clear early and Ceroc is unable to match his stride, allowing a lone pacesetter to control tempo and conserve enough to last home.
scenarios.body: Rockonliam's two recent wins both came on Good ground over 20f and he has the form profile to suggest he can dominate if given a soft lead; De Bromhead and O'Keeffe connecting in a Grade-level form run is a serious platform. The shorter trip relative to those around him in the field and strong handler stats (T14: 4/31) make front-running solo domination a live danger at this price.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse, Closers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel between Rockonliam and Ceroc is fierce enough to bring the whole field into a messy, strung-out affair where late-staying types benefit most.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Duty Bound and Teenage Kiss being repositioned further back than natural and actually delivering a late run — both are redistributed prominent types and not genuine hold-up horses, which markedly reduces the credibility of a closing finish. Only if the front two truly blow up entirely would any rear-of-field finisher get into this.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage, Attrition Race
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground proves more demanding than the going report suggests and jumping errors reduce the field, leaving the most resolute stayer to grind it out.
scenarios.body: A 3m1f chase with competitive weights and multiple pace angles creates carnage risk; Ceroc's recent P-runs and Sphagnum's 0-run in latest start hint at vulnerability. Whichever runner produces the cleanest round of jumping and carries a light weight to the last is best placed — Rue Taylor (156lbs, 3 recent wins on similar going) or Jacovec Cavern both have the durability profile.

watchPoints.text: Ceroc's two non-completion runs (P entries in 52F-P5 form) make him a live jumping risk at 3m1f if Rockonliam forces a fierce early pace — watch Enright for any signs of Ceroc being outpaced into fences in the first mile.
Rockonliam must handle a significant trip extension from 20f to 26f; if his stamina fails after the third-last, the race could open dramatically for Jacovec Cavern or Rue Taylor tracking just behind.

Teenage Kiss and Duty Bound are both natural prominent racers pushed into unnatural positions — watch for both to drift forward from the flag despite their mapped positions, potentially creating more early congestion than the two confirmed front-runners alone would generate.

Sphagnum's latest run was a 0 (pulled up or fell, unspecified) which is unexplained — watch for any paddock signs of soundness or wellbeing before accepting the form at face value on a step back up in trip.

Good ground is consistent across the entire Wexford card — no going drift to worry about, but the uniform surface means class and jumping accuracy will separate these runners rather than any ground bias or slog factor.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Solsbury Hill
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse trained by Conor O'Dwyer, ridden by Charlie O'Dwyer (3lb claim); won last time out 39 days ago over 16f on Good and carries a strong sim-going record (11/14, 2W3P), but at 1m7½f needs the pace to be genuine enough to allow a late run from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Solsbury Hill shaped with promise when winning and has run over today's trip and conditions before, with our rating marking him down as the pick of seven here; the unseating last time out is the obvious question-mark he must answer.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer with a strong Good-ground record (13/15, 3W8P) who won over 16f in his most recent outing 32 days ago; trainer Martin Hassett has a modest recent strike rate (0/3 in 14 days) and the horse will need a searching gallop to produce his best from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Bynx has shown she can win at this level, scoring two starts back and again four starts back in recent form, and she returns on 32 days' rest with distance and going experience in her favour — her last two runs disappoint, but the winning profile makes her hard to oppose here.

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter here, he drops back to a prominent role from recent runs over 2m4f-plus and is the key shape-setter; his STYLE_FIT tag (0.94) reflects that dictating over this shorter trip is not his most natural groove, though the lack of a challenger means he will likely control the tempo regardless.
runners_data.comment: Ned In The Park arrives here just 11 days after unseating, yet boasts a second two starts back and a third three starts back, showing consistent placing form; winless in his last five starts, the 161 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old has a spotless sim-going record (7/7, 1W3P) and arrives on 17 days' rest with Darragh O'Keeffe aboard — a strong combination — but her natural hold-up style means she is placed in midfield on the map only because the rear is congested; her STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence she secures ideal ground.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Lady Doyanne brings solid each-way claims having finished second and third in her last two outings, and she has run over today's distance and going before — the concern is a hefty 158 lb to carry while still winless in her last five.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer (OR 105) with two wins and three places from 15 runs on similar going; returns quickly on 11 days' rest but that is not unusual for this yard, and racing just off Ned In The Park in second or third makes this trip and setup look straightforward on paper.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out after a win three starts back, Kilbrin Rocco has run over today's trip and going, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures and carrying 157 lb, he is hard to fancy off the back of that latest ninth.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's seven-year-old won over 16f on Good 17 days ago and has a solid sim-going profile (10/11, 2W4P); a natural hold-up horse whose position in the midfield mapping is a function of the crowded rear rather than a reflection of how he will actually race, which tempers his claims in a slow-run scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ballybrittas won last time out and returns on a quick 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, though a carrying weight of 156 lb and just one win in his last five starts being the exception rather than the rule suggest he faces a stiff test here.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner (OR 96) with a claim jockey (Kevin Healy, 7lb) and a tongue-tie; finished second over this course and distance trip on Good last time, which is an obvious positive, and his prominent style suits the likely race shape, though inconsistent form (63F0/2) demands a clean round of jumping.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked last on our figures, Rightfolksplace has a fall on his record three starts back, though a second last time out and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement under 148 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Ned In The Park is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner handicap chase over 1m7½f on Good ground at Wexford, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he should dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the front. Kilbrin Rocco and Rightfolksplease will push forward to dispute second and third early, creating a functional but not pressured pace that is unlikely to stretch the field significantly through the early stages. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically sit in their natural position — Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded in this race shape, and neither is likely to secure their preferred ground at the back of the field. With Ned In The Park setting a controlled tempo unchallenged, this race shape most favours prominent racers who can travel fluidly just off the lead and pounce from a handy position, rather than true hold-up horses who will need a pace injection that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ned In The Park Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Ned In The Park travels comfortably and sets a controlled lead that no rival is able to challenge or disrupt.
scenarios.body: Ned In The Park dictates throughout on a comfortable lead, the pace stays honest but not fast, and horses who travel prominently into the straight are best placed to land a blow; hold-up types get an insufficient test and lack the fuel to finish through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbrin Rocco or Rightfolksplease push Ned In The Park for the lead and a competitive early gallop develops among the front three.
scenarios.body: A genuine contest for the lead lifts the pace and tests stamina more rigorously, and those who travel prominently but with cover just off the front rank are best positioned to benefit when rivals cry enough; the hold-up horses still struggle to find sufficient momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Ned In The Park is genuinely searching and hold-up types find the racing room to finish through.
scenarios.body: Solsbury Hill or Bynx, coming from off the pace, would need the tempo to have emptied the front rank and a clean run into the straight to produce a telling late surge; the redistribution of Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas means the true hold-up profile is underrepresented and less likely to deliver.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race order and create an unpredictable finish from an unusual position.
scenarios.body: A chase at a right-handed track like Wexford at a sharp distance invites jumping mishaps, and any disruption to Ned In The Park's rhythm could scramble the race shape entirely; Ballybrittas or Lady Doyanne, shuffled forward by circumstance, could benefit from positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Ned In The Park's jumping must be monitored closely — if he makes a significant error early he loses the lead and his entire tactical advantage evaporates, scrambling the race shape for every other runner.

Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas are natural hold-up horses who will be pushed forward out of their comfort zone by the race shape; if either loses their position and drifts to the rear, they face a materially worse chance than their form figures suggest.
Kilbrin Rocco returns on just 11 days' rest; if any fitness shortfall shows in the latter stages of a race that stays honest rather than truly searching, his chance fades at a crucial moment.

The Good ground is consistent across the card and genuinely in play for all runners — no horse carries a significant going concern, but the sharper Wexford track rewards accurate jumping, and any errors at the fences could cost lengths in a small field where every position counts.

races.name: Racing Again 28th August Fillies Flat Race

runners_data.name: Alicious
runners_data.comment: Alicious arrives on debut with no public form to go on, but connections are firing at 26% in the last 14 days, and this unexposed filly — carrying 159 lb — is open to any amount of improvement as she steps into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Dancing Symbol
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore completely unexposed, Dancing Symbol makes her debut carrying 159 lb — an unknown quantity with everything still to prove, but open to any amount of improvement as connections get their first look at her under rules.

runners_data.name: Hee Hiles
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore completely unexposed, Hee Hiles makes her debut carrying 159 lb — an open-to-improvement type whose potential remains unknown until she steps into the racecourse spotlight for the first time.

runners_data.name: Highland Call
runners_data.comment: Highland Call is unexposed and open to improvement after just one recorded run, an eighth that start, and steps up here carrying 159 lb. Yet to win, she remains lightly raced enough to hold untapped potential worth keeping onside.

runners_data.name: Honey Buck's
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Honey Buck's was runner-up last time out and remains yet to win, but that sole start hints at plenty more to come; she returns after 29 days carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: La Muleta
runners_data.comment: La Muleta returns after 92 days off having finished second last time out, and as a lightly raced filly yet to win she remains unexposed and open to improvement on that encouraging effort, carrying 159 lb here.

runners_data.name: Misses Woo
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Misses Woo returns after 83 days off carrying 159 lb, yet to score in recent starts; lightly raced, she holds obvious potential for better with that sole run barely scratching the surface.

runners_data.name: Prometteuse
runners_data.comment: Prometteuse makes her debut carrying 159 lb — unexposed and an unknown quantity, but lightly raced profiles can surprise, and there is plenty of room for improvement as connections find out what she has to offer.

runners_data.name: Sierra's Dream
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore a completely unknown quantity on debut, Sierra's Dream is unexposed and open to any amount of improvement; carrying 159 lb, she is one to watch as her true potential reveals itself over time.

runners_data.name: The Lodge Lane
runners_data.comment: Unraced and completely unexposed, The Lodge Lane steps into the unknown on debut carrying 159 lb, with her slate blank and improvement entirely possible — a filly to watch as her career begins.
